standard.title: Design physical activity strategies
standard.description: design and justify strategies to increase physical activity levels to achieve health and wellbeing outcomes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have proposed and explained strategies to increase physical activity and reduce sedentary behaviour (Y5-6). They can describe what strategies might work but have not yet been expected to design and justify strategies against specific health and wellbeing outcome targets.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students design and justify strategies to increase physical activity levels to achieve health and wellbeing outcomes.

nodes.label: Identifying physical activity barriers and enablers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify factors that support or limit physical activity participation for themselves and their peer group, including personal, social and environmental factors.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two factors (personal, social or environmental) that influence their own physical activity levels.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and categorise factors that support and limit physical activity participation across personal, social and environmental domains; compare their current activity levels with Australia's 24-Hour Movement Guidelines; identify specific gaps.
wider: Compare physical activity levels, sleep and sedentary time against the 24-Hour Movement Guidelines and map personal and social factors contributing to any identified gaps
Investigate which physical activities different peer groups engage in for social and emotional wellbeing, identifying patterns in motivation and participation
nodes.hinge_reason: Design decisions require a clear understanding of what is being designed against — students who cannot identify the specific barriers and enablers in their own context will produce generic strategies with no real justification grounded in evidence.

response_modes.reason: Use a structured analysis framework (personal/social/environmental) to ensure students map their own context systematically before designing. Strategies should be explicitly linked to identified barriers.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two factors that influence their own physical activity participation
Categorises factors as personal, social or environmental

nodes.label: Understanding health and wellbeing outcomes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the health and wellbeing outcomes that increased physical activity is intended to achieve, with reference to specific outcome areas (physical, social, emotional, mental).
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one health or wellbeing outcome that increased physical activity can support and explain the link.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how increased physical activity contributes to outcomes across physical, social, emotional and mental wellbeing dimensions; connect activity types to specific outcomes; use the 24-Hour Movement Guidelines as a reference point.
wider: Investigate how physical activity supports emotional and social wellbeing specifically — examining the evidence for social connection and mood benefits beyond physical fitness outcomes
Research how sedentary behaviour alongside insufficient activity creates compounding health risks, and use this understanding to justify targeting both in a strategy

response_modes.reason: Justification requires specific outcome understanding — width here means connecting a range of outcome types to different activity strategies rather than knowing one outcome type deeply.

success_criteria: Names at least one health or wellbeing outcome that increased physical activity supports
Explains the link between a specific activity type and the outcome named

nodes.label: Designing and justifying strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can design a strategy to increase physical activity levels for themselves or others, with explicit justification linking design decisions to identified barriers and targeted health or wellbeing outcomes.
nodes.minimum_width: Design one strategy to increase physical activity and justify at least one design decision by linking it to an identified barrier or health/wellbeing outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Design a realistic personal or peer-targeted physical activity strategy addressing multiple barriers and targeting specific health and wellbeing outcomes; justify each key design decision with reference to evidence; include monitoring or evaluation mechanisms.
wider: Design and monitor a personal physical activity plan over multiple weeks, evaluating whether the strategy achieved the intended wellbeing outcomes and revising it accordingly

Design an activity program for a specific peer group (e.g. students who prefer non-competitive activities) with explicit justification for design decisions tailored to that group's barriers and preferences

response_modes.reason: Design and justify integrates barrier analysis, outcome understanding, and strategic planning into one coherent artefact. Instruction should scaffold the full design-justify cycle rather than treating design as the endpoint.
Justification quality increases when students have a range of health/wellbeing outcome types to draw on. Width in outcome knowledge directly improves justification depth.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who design for a range of purposes and justify against multiple outcome types develop a genuinely transferable health literacy capability applicable to personal health decisions well beyond this unit.
success_criteria: Designs a strategy to increase physical activity levels for themselves or others
Justifies at least one design decision by linking it to an identified barrier or a specific health/wellbeing outcome
Identifies a realistic way to monitor or evaluate the strategy's effectiveness
